prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, transforming the analysis of who trades, how productivity responds to openness, and the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: B020 stays first for me. Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting turned trade from an industry-level into a firm-level subject. It added within-industry reallocation as a channel for productivity gains, and it made firm-level microdata central to estimating and evaluating trade. The Melitz (2003) model and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extension to exporting versus FDI are a widely used workhorse in trade, industrial organization and quantitative macro. More than two decades of replication and extension support maturity. The core contribution is conceptual rather than only a data or method tool, and it has measurable consequences for empirical practice and policy. It complements rather than repeats the 2008 recognition of new trade theory. The Helpman-Melitz pairing follows the clearest lines of credit on the ballot entry.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is attribution. The credited list omits Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, whose firm-level evidence and models are close to the core, and a prize built on the Melitz framework alone would leave that boundary contestable. Helpman is also credited on B001 for a different body of work, so the Committee must decide which contribution it is recognizing. Redding's later quantitative and spatial extensions would also be left out. Some gains-from-trade results depend on parametric assumptions, such as the Pareto productivity distribution.

responses.point: B001 (Grossman and Helpman) is the first-ranked candidate, with a clean two-person attribution, decades of confirmation, and no timing concern. Empirical validation of the lobbying models is mixed, and trade was recognized in 2008.
responses.response: I agree that the Grossman-Helpman attribution is cleaner than B020, and I keep B001 as an alternative. The two cases differ in what the work changed. Protection for sale is influential mainly as theory, and Tommy's own note on mixed empirical validation is the reason I rank it below B020. Melitz-type models changed how trade is measured and how policy is evaluated with firm data. I would not give a trade prize to both strands in one year, so the Committee should choose between them rather than combine them. I put the larger weight on B020 because its empirical footprint is wider.

responses.point: Richard ranked B020 first but flagged a real attribution gap, because Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited. He also noted that Helpman's overlap with B001 forces a choice about which body of work is recognized.
responses.response: I share both concerns and flagged the same gap in my opening. Given the credited names, I think Helpman and Melitz are still defensible. The Melitz framework is the widely adopted workhorse, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple is the natural extension. The gap is real, though, and I would count it as a risk to this configuration rather than a minor footnote. The Committee should decide whether it is disqualifying, because we cannot repair it by adding uncredited names. I lean towards 'no' but hold that view with moderate confidence. On the Helpman overlap, I would recognize him for the firm-heterogeneity work and treat B001 as an alternative, not as a second claim in the same year.

responses.point: Per ranked B016 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) first as a field-defining political-economics programme. He proposed Gertler as a third name on B031, alongside Kiyotaki and Moore, for the financial accelerator.
responses.response: I take the B016 case seriously, since it is why I ranked B016 third. My reservations are the thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize and the contested identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons. On B031, I would keep the pair Kiyotaki and Moore. Their collateral-amplification mechanism is a sharply attributable contribution. The financial accelerator is a related strand with Bernanke, who is already a laureate, and adding Gertler blurs a clean attribution without strengthening the scientific case. I also note that Per and I are frequent co-authors, so this disagreement should be read with that in mind.

responses.point: Anna ranked B019 first, crediting Autor, Hanson and Dorn for credibly identified trade-shock evidence that changed the labour-demand and inequality debate. She sees Katz as a possible alternative third name.
responses.response: I agree that the design-based China-shock evidence is strong and has had very high policy influence. Reading her argument and the other openings, I accept that the China-shock core is best attributed to Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and my opening choice of Katz in that slot was a judgment call about the task and skill-premium strand. I still rank B019 below B020 because of the continuing debate about the magnitude and persistence of the effects and the overlap with the task literature of scholars outside the credited list. It is a strong alternative that I did not name among my two, because I rank B001 and B031 slightly higher.

uncertainties: Whether the Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum contribution is close enough to the core that omitting them undermines a B020 award.
Whether the Committee would treat Helpman's B020 and B001 contributions as one body of work or choose between them.
How much weight the Committee gives to Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions relative to the originating framework.
The size of the gains-from-trade results under alternative productivity distributions and parametric assumptions.
Whether the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises reduces the marginal case for B031 more than I have assumed.
statement.conflict_note: The profile shows no connection to the credited names on B020, my preferred part. The profile does show a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow, who is credited on shortlisted B036 (not part of my configuration). It also shows frequent co-authorship with Per Krusell and co-authorship with John Hassler, both of whom ranked B016 and B031 in their top three. These connections may need recusal consideration. They are disclosed, not adjudicated.
